html:
SMTO-MEM-0008 — One of this memory's tags isn't allowed

GUID: 22bc5532-2c30-4341-904c-a58253f0abae
Slug: memory-invalid-tag
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: mem

What happened

  • SMTO didn't save this memory because a tag (a label that helps find it) has characters SMTO doesn't accept or is too long, or there are more than 32 tags. Nothing was saved or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the Memory Editor, edit Tags so each tag uses only letters, numbers, periods, underscores, colons or hyphens, with commas between tags and no spaces inside a tag. A tag containing any other character, such as a space or a slash, is rejected.
  2. Keep each tag to 64 characters or fewer and use no more than 32 tags, then select Save. SMTO limits tag length and count, and going over either limit stops the save.
  3. If the agent hit this while saving a memory, ask it to save again using a few short tags, such as project or preferences. The agent chose those tags itself, and simple tags let the save go through.

What success looks like

  • The memory shows Saved, and its tags appear in the Memory Editor's tag filter.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the tags you tried, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep saving the same tags unchanged; they will be rejected every time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Memory tag validation (normalize_tag/normalize_tags) rejected the tags: a tag does not match ^[a-zA-Z0-9._:-]{1,64}$, or tags is not a list or has more than 32 items.

What this means

  • A tag violates the 1–64-character ASCII grammar or tags is not a list within the 32-tag input bound. Memory validation and conditional writes preserve the current stored revision on rejection. This is global Memory, separate from conversation KV; diagnostic rendering does not perform additional storage operations.

Why this can happen

  • A tag violates the 1–64-character ASCII grammar or tags is not a list within the 32-tag input bound.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the input tag list before normalization/deduplication and each tag's length/characters.

How to fix it

  • Pass tags as a list of at most 32 ASCII strings, each 1–64 characters from letters, digits, '.', '_', ':' or '-' (stored lowercased and deduplicated). See normalize_tag and normalize_tags in src/agent_runtime/skills/memory/models.py.
  • Use supported ASCII tags within the advertised per-tag length and tag-count limits.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported bounded tags normalize consistently for the intended entry.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Memory validation and conditional writes preserve the current stored revision on rejection. This is global Memory, separate from conversation KV; diagnostic rendering does not perform additional storage operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
